title: Post-Doctoral Researcher, PhD, DeepMind, 2026 Start (Fixed-Term Contract)
descriptionHtml:
The Post-doctoral Researcher role is a 12 to 24-month role designed to explore challenging problems for pushing frontiers of AI, while collaborating with DeepMind scientists and engineers. Your role will entail conducting human-computer interaction (HCI) research on how people interact with, oversee, and provide feedback to increasingly autonomous AI agents, designing and building novel interfaces and interaction techniques for human-agent collaboration, and evaluating them through rigorous user studies. Insights from your work will inform how agents learn from human feedback and remain safe and aligned with human intent, with potential application to products that might have a positive impact on billions of users.

At DeepMind, we're a team of scientists, engineers, machine learning experts and more, working together to advance the state of the art in artificial intelligence, and fulfill our mission of building AI responsibility to benefit humanity. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, and collaborate with others on critical challenges, ensuring safety and ethics are the highest priority.

In particular, our AQUA team at DeepMind India works at the frontier of AI agents, focusing on autonomous self-improvement, reinforcement learning, and the safety and alignment of agents. We build agents that continually improve themselves by learning from their own experience, interactions, and feedback, and we develop methods to ensure that increasingly capable and autonomous agents remain safe, reliable, and aligned with human intent and values. We aim to bring our research into Google's cutting-edge models and products, while also disseminating our findings through publications at top ML conferences/journals.

Responsibilities

  • Work with research mentors to formulate research projects or novel applications of machine learning aligned with the team's mission. Conduct research and publish high quality work.
  • Design and execute large-scale experiments, writing high-quality, reusable code, and contributing to a production-ready system using frameworks such as JAX. Learn and understand research in machine learning algorithms.
  • Understand how to use research to drive design decisions. Design and conduct user studies (e.g. interviews, surveys, controlled experiments, and field deployments) to understand how people interact with, oversee, and provide feedback to AI agents.
  • Prototype novel interfaces and interaction techniques that help people steer, supervise, and collaborate with increasingly autonomous agents. Develop human-centered evaluation methods and metrics for the helpfulness, trustworthiness, safety, and alignment of agents.
  • Translate insights from human studies into improvements in how agents learn from human feedback and improve themselves (e.g. reward modeling, preference elicitation, and human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning).

Minimum qualifications:

  • PhD degree in a STEM field (e.g., Computer Science, Mathematics, or Statistics) or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience with one or more general purpose programming languages: Python, C/C++, or Java, etc. and training deep learning models in frameworks such as JAX, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
  • Research experience in machine learning or AI techniques (e.g., open source project(s), campus lab experience, research internship(s), or publication(s)).
  • One or more scientific publication submission(s) in AI conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, CVPR, ICCV, ICLR).

Preferred qualifications:

  • PhD and Master’s degree in a STEM field (e.g. Computer Science, Mathematics, or Statistics) or equivalent practical experience.
  • Hands-on experience with one or more general purpose programming languages: Python, C/C++, or Java, etc and training deep learning models in frameworks such as JAX, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
  • Extensive research experience in machine learning or AI techniques (e.g. open source project(s), campus lab experience, research internship(s), or publication(s)).
  • Ability to work and collaborate across multiple teams and work with ambiguity.
  • A strong publication record in top-tier conferences/journals.

title: Customer Onboarding Strategist, ANZ Market, Google Customer Solutions (Cantonese)

title: Reverse Engineer, Mandiant FLARE
descriptionHtml:

title: Data Center Technician III
descriptionHtml:

As an Operations Technician, you'll install, configure, test, troubleshoot and maintain hardware (like servers and its components) and server software (like Google's Linux cluster). You'll also take on the configuration of more complex components such as networks, routers, hubs, bridges, switches and networking protocols. You'll participate in or lead small project teams on larger installations and develop project contingency plans. A typical day involves manual movement and installation of racks, and while it can sometimes be physically demanding, you are excited to work with infrastructure that is at the cutting-edge of computer technology.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

descriptionHtml:

In this role, you will work cross-functionally to guide products from conception to launch by connecting the technical and business worlds. You can break down complex problems into steps that drive product development.

In Google Search, we're reimagining what it means to search for information – any way and anywhere. To do that, we need to solve complex engineering challenges and expand our infrastructure, while maintaining a universally accessible and useful experience that people around the world rely on. In joining the Search team, you'll have an opportunity to make an impact on billions of people globally.

title: Security Engineer, Cloud Vulnerability Response
descriptionHtml:
Our Security team works to create and maintain the safest operating environment for Google's users and developers. Security Engineers work with network equipment and actively monitor our systems for attacks and intrusions. In this role, you will also work with software engineers to proactively identify and fix security flaws and vulnerabilities.

Cloud Vulnerability Coordination leads Google Cloud’s response to its most critical security vulnerabilities. We partner across engineering, security research, communications, and legal teams to drive fast, unified responses to high-stakes product vulnerabilities, including embargoed, zero-day, and critical third-party threats, while managing coordinated disclosures, CVEs, and customer notifications. As AI accelerates both discovery and exploitation, our team ensures Google Cloud and its customers stay ahead of emerging risks.

In this role, you will join the Cloud Vulnerability Coordination team within Google Cloud. As a Vulnerability Response Security Engineer, you will serve as the technical anchor for Google Cloud's response to critical and embargoed product vulnerabilities, protecting customer trust through fast, technically sound action. Working alongside product engineering and central security response teams, you will assess real-world exposure, triage severe flaws, and guide teams toward verified mitigations and fixes. Based in Sydney, you will provide critical global coverage during APAC hours in a follow-the-sun model, with the autonomy to investigate emerging issues independently before handing off across global shifts. Beyond live response, you will invest in long-term scale by building automation, dependency-tracking pipelines, and AI-assisted triage workflows so our operations keep pace with compressing threat timelines.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Responsibilities

  • Act as incident commander rapidly triaging high-severity and embargoed vulnerabilities across Google Cloud, setting response priorities, directing product engineering, security, legal, and communications teams, partnering with central security response teams on cross-company events.
  • Investigate critical flaws in Google Cloud services and shared dependencies, read code and deployment configurations, and evaluate the effectiveness of proposed mitigations and patches.
  • Design, build, and maintain software tools and AI-assisted workflows that integrate with central security response systems and platform data for automated impact analysis, dependency-to-owner mapping, and triage verification.
  • Partner with product engineering, central security, and communications teams to confirm remediations are complete and risk assessments, executive updates, and customer security advisories are technically accurate.
  • Lead technical retrospectives on vulnerability events to surface architectural, telemetry, and response gaps, and partner with platform and central security engineering teams.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience in vulnerability response, incident response, or security engineering.
  • Experience leading technical vulnerability investigations, root-cause analyses, and cross-team remediation in enterprise or cloud environments.
  • Experience programming or scripting in one or more general-purpose languages (e.g., Python, Go).

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience acting as incident or response commander for high-severity vulnerabilities and security events under time pressure.
  • Experience reading and reviewing code to assess exploitability and validate fixes.
  • Experience building AI-assisted, agentic, or automated workflows for vulnerability management and security operations.
  • Understanding of cloud computing architecture, container and VM infrastructure, secure system design, and software supply chains, including dependency analysis.
  • Ability to explain technical vulnerabilities, exploit mechanics, and risk clearly to both engineers and executive leadership.

title: Lead Analyst, Frontier Safety
descriptionHtml:

They use technical know-how, excellent problem-solving skills, user insights, and proactive communication to protect users and our partners from abuse across Google products like Search, Maps, Gmail, and Google Ads. On this team, you're a big-picture thinker and strategic team-player with a passion for doing what’s right. You work globally and cross-functionally with Google engineers and product managers to identify and fight abuse and fraud cases at Google speed - with urgency. And you take pride in knowing that every day you are working hard to promote trust in Google and ensuring the highest levels of user safety.

The Content Adversarial Red Team (CART) in Trust and Safety conducts adversarial testing of Google’s Generative AI models, product surfaces, and autonomous agents to uncover vulnerabilities, jailbreaks, and emerging catastrophic risks not identified in standard evaluations.

In this Lead Trust and Safety Analyst role, you will serve as the Senior Dual-Domain Frontier Safety (FS) Analytic Expert (CBRN and Cyber) and evaluation lead. Bringing deep subject-matter expertise in Frontier Safety threats, you will design, direct, and conduct complex red-teaming assessments to evaluate high-consequence capability uplift risks across Google's AI products. Operating with high autonomy across multi-quarter strategic horizons, you will anchor CART's Frontier Safety red-teaming program (~70%) while partnering with sibling RAIT teams (SCALE and Novel) (~30%).

In this collaboration, you will calibrate automated product-surface evaluators (autoraters), evolve dynamic attack trees, define threat personas for multi-turn/agentic simulators, and lead Tier-1 product loss triage. At Google we work hard to earn our users’ trust every day. Trust & Safety is Google’s team of abuse fighting and user trust experts working daily to make the internet a safer place. We partner with teams across Google to deliver bold solutions in abuse areas such as malware, spam and account hijacking. A team of Analysts, Policy Specialists, Engineers, and Program Managers, we work to reduce risk and fight abuse across all of Google’s products, protecting our users, advertisers, and publishers across the globe in over 40 languages.Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Learn more about benefits at Google.

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Security Engineer, Enterprise SaaS Security
descriptionHtml:
There's no such thing as a "safe system" - only safer systems. Our Security team works to create and maintain the safest operating environment for Google's users and developers. As a Security Engineer, you help protect network boundaries, keep computer systems and network devices hardened against attacks and provide security services to protect highly sensitive data like passwords and customer information. Security Engineers work directly with network equipment and actively monitor our systems for attacks and intrusions. You also work with software engineers to proactively identify and fix security flaws and vulnerabilities.

You use your industry experience to own and drive the resolution of complex security incidents, policy questions and technical security issues.

As a Senior Security Engineer on this team, you will act as a technical leader and mentor. You will be responsible for securing Google’s enterprise usage of third-party Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platforms. You will help scale our capacity for incoming security vulnerabilities, build automated tooling to reduce manual workloads using AI, and drive risk insights and remediations. You will ensure all new SaaS launches are secure by performing security assessments and ensure the adoption of required security controls. You will mentor and guide other engineers, fostering a collaborative environment to achieve collective goals. With your technical foundation and exceptional cross-functional collaboration skills, you will manage complex security issues and operations. You will have a breadth of application security experience such as SaaS or cloud security, API security, authentication and access control, threat modeling, conducting security assessments, etc.

The Core team builds the technical foundation behind Google’s flagship products. We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. These are the essential building blocks for excellent, safe, and coherent experiences for our users and drive the pace of innovation for every developer. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end security strategy for high-risk third-party SaaS platforms, identifying and driving solutions for complex, ambiguous security issues.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior engineers, guiding the development of scalable security controls and fostering a culture of engineering excellence.
  • Architect and engineer advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) solutions, leveraging AI/ML automation to reduce manual toil and improve operational visibility.
  • Lead complex, cross-functional security assessments to derive actionable risk insights, ensuring Google's enterprise usage of SaaS remains resilient against evolving threats.
  • Influence the broader SaaS security roadmap by collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to define policies and drive the adoption of required security controls.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience with security assessments or security design reviews or threat modeling.
  • 5 years of experience with security engineering, computer and network security and security protocols.
  • 5 years of coding experience in one or more languages (Python, Go, SQL, Javascript).
  • 1 year of experience leading teams in a technical capacity or leading technical risk analysis in an enterprise environment.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Understanding of federated AuthN/AuthZ technologies (SAML, SCIM, OIDC).
  • Understanding of networking concepts (protocols, topologies, encryption).
  • Ability to perform technical security assessments of large complex systems.
  • Ability to design and develop new security control implementations.

title: Financial Analyst, Compute Infrastructure Business
descriptionHtml:

title: Senior IP Design Verification Engineer, Google Cloud
descriptionHtml:
In this role, you’ll work to shape the future of AI/ML hardware acceleration. In this role, you will own the full verification life-cycle from verification planning and test execution to coverage closure, with an emphasis on meeting stringent AI/ML performance and accuracy goals, build constrained-random verification environments capable of exposing corner-case bugs and ensuring the reliability of Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) workloads on Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) hardware. title: Program Manager III, Logistics Capacity Planning, Cloud Logistics
descriptionHtml:
A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Program Manager at Google, you’ll lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish — working with stakeholders to plan requirements, manage project schedules, identify risks, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. Your projects will often span offices, time zones, and hemispheres. It's your job to coordinate the players and keep them up to date on progress and deadlines.

The Google Cloud Logistics (GCL) Capacity Planning team ensures the operational readiness and scalability of Google's global logistics network. In this role, you will own end-to-end capacity planning, transforming demand forecasts into executable operational plans. You will bridge supply chain strategy and on-the-ground execution by designing and owning the quantitative models that govern network flow, storage, throughput, and labor. You will use SQL, data pipelines, and analytical models to simulate sourcing changes, stress-test network capacity (e.g., space, dock throughput, labor), and run scenarios to balance workloads. You will establish and lead planning cycles, including regional Demand-Supply Reviews (DSR) with Operations and third-party logistics (3PL) partners, integrating commitments into monthly S&OP/D&OP processes. You will also partner with Engineering and Product teams as a subject matter expert to codify business logic and network constraints into automated, scalable planning tools.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $159000 - $230000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Build network flow and distribution models across upstream suppliers, regional fulfillment hubs, and destination data centers; evaluate sourcing rule changes, lane realignments, and routing adjustments to assess downstream capacity impacts and balance network workload.
  • Establish and govern repeatable capacity planning processes, planning calendars, and forecast lock cycles from the ground up, embedding warehouse and data center capacity plans into monthly S&OP/D&OP cycles, rolling commits, and quarterly/annual budgeting.
  • Own key forecast health metrics, including plan-vs-actual variance and forecast accuracy/bias (WAPE, MAPE), driving root-cause analysis and continuous calibration of the underlying models and parameters that enable constraint planning.
  • Design, build, and own forecasting and capacity models that enable constraint planning across GCL global warehouses and data centers, translating upstream supply chain and deployment schedules into multi-horizon plans across storage space, dock throughput, and labor.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience in program or project management.
  • Experience in developing forecasting models and scripting in SQL.
  • Experience in logistics, logistics capacity planning, network modeling, constraint planning, or demand forecasting.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience building and owning end-to-end quantitative logistics capacity, network, constraint, or forecasting models across warehousing, distribution centers, data center operations, or hardware supply chains.
  • Expertise in physical logistics capacity and distribution planning, modeling network flows, sourcing rule changes, storage footprint, dock throughput, and labor capacity across short and long-term horizons.
  • Advanced proficiency in SQL, Python, or statistical modeling tools to build capacity pipelines, simulate network/sourcing changes, analyze plan-vs-actual variances, and improve forecast accuracy (WAPE, MAPE, Bias).
  • Define business logic, sourcing rules, and functional requirements that integrate and automate manual planning models into internal logistics capacity planning tooling.
